name: WA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Challenger Mary Silva has raised under $9,000 with about $1,300 on hand, versus $4.3 million raised and $1 million on hand for incumbent Suzan DelBene
District leans Democratic by 15 points and DelBene is a sitting incumbent
No public polls or expert ratings exist; prediction markets price a Democratic win around 95 percent
A Republican-tilted national environment is the only force pointing the other way
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Democratic lean, DelBene's incumbency, and a fundraising gap of roughly 500-to-1 leave the challenger without the resources to run a competitive campaign, and markets price a Democratic win near certainty.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending against DelBene or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow the margin, though the money disparity makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Suzan DelBene, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a Seattle-area district that leans Democratic by fifteen points. Her campaign has raised more than $4.2 million and holds over $1 million on hand, while Republican Mary Silva has reported under $9,000 in contributions and roughly $1,300 in cash. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 95 percent.

The fundamentals point the same direction: the district's partisan lean, DelBene's incumbency, and the lopsided money race all favor her. A national environment tilted toward Republicans could narrow the margin somewhat, but with the challenger lacking the resources to compete, the seat remains safely in Democratic hands barring an unforeseen development.
